key_insight: Drug-safety warnings were weaker than English in eight of nine language-by-risk comparisons across Russian, Arabic and Hebrew Wikipedia, but estimates were uncertain.
clinical_relevance: Readers seeking drug-safety information may encounter different levels of actionable warning across Wikipedia languages.
method: Audited 33 drugs across four languages: 24 risk-positive drugs and nine negative controls.
Three large language models scored warnings as absent, mentioned or explicit directives across G6PD deficiency, teratogenicity and QT prolongation.
Used a hierarchical Bayesian model with English as reference; a pharmacist resolved disagreements in two risk domains.
evidence_signal: Pooled cumulative odds ratios versus English were 0.41 for Russian, 0.25 for Arabic and 0.31 for Hebrew; all 95% credible intervals included 1.
watch_item: The small, purposively selected drug panel and LLM codes not yet validated against human coding limit confidence and generalizability.
paper_title: Drug Safety Warnings in English, Russian, Arabic and Hebrew Wikipedia: A Cross-Sectional Audit of 33 Drugs Across Three Risk Domains
